answer.answer: The NPS Vatsalya Scheme is a contributory saving and long-term financial security scheme designed exclusively for minors below 18 years of age [E01]. It was announced by the Finance Minister in the Union Budget for FY 2024-25 and is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) [E01]. The scheme allows parents or guardians to open accounts for their children with a minimum contribution of ₹250 per year with no maximum limit [E01]. Relatives and friends can also gift contributions [E01]. Parents/guardians can choose any registered pension fund to manage investments [E01]. Upon turning 18, subscribers can continue for up to three years (until age 21) unless they opt to exit or shift to another NPS model [E01]. Partial withdrawals up to 25% of contributions (excluding returns) are allowed after 3 years for education, specified illnesses, or disability over 75% [E01][E02]. Upon exit at age 18, up to 80% of accumulated corpus can be withdrawn as a lump sum, with the balance used for annuity purchase; if the corpus is less than ₹8 Lakh, the entire amount can be withdrawn [E02][E03]. The scheme promotes financial discipline, early savings habits, and offers tax benefits [E03].
